scope: Original 2020 Dune: Imperium standard base 2–4-player multiplayer, including required two-player House Hagal. Solo, variants, expansions, promos, and Uprising excluded.
conclusion: The 69-question benchmark covers the distinct in-scope procedures, outcome branches, and consequential timing/exception interactions stated by the supplied rulebook and official FAQ. This independent challenge found no qualifying addition and no material correction to the fixed answers.

sources_read.extent: Complete in-scope text, main PDF pages 1–19; page 20 solo procedures excluded from assessment.
Visually inspected pp17–18 Board Space Guide and p19 House Hagal, including graphical access icons, Combat labels, exchange rates, and two-player setup.
All four pages, both columns; assessed base-game clauses only. The 2025-01-13 official FAQ supersedes old Mentat reward timing.
All Q01–Q69 fixed answers and source references; grading policy and terminology notes.
All accepted novelty claims, rejected candidates, source mappings, and ledger status. Ledger claims were checked against source and literal question requirements.

independence: No summary, reader response, grade, audit, or previous reviewer report was read. The expressly requested coverage ledger was read.

findings.finding: Ordinary human turn alternation and ordinary untied Combat rewards are explicitly required now. The earlier-looking source-map rows do not by themselves demonstrate these rules, but the later ledger mappings and actual Q68/Q69 do. No residual gap remains.
source_references: Main PDF p8 Phase 2: Player Turns

findings.finding: The key correctly gives Sort Through the Chaos Mentat acquisition at the start of the next round rather than retaining the obsolete immediate-acquisition/keep-through-Recall wording in main PDF p16.
source_references: Official FAQ p4 Sort Through the Chaos

findings.finding: Two-player House Hagal is correctly treated as a non-scoring spoiler with three Agents, no initial garrison, no normal board effects or resource collection, no Conflict rewards or control acquisition, and permitted Alliance possession. Guild Envoy and the solo-only Signet/reward/difficulty procedures are correctly excluded.
source_references: Main PDF p19 general and Two-Player Games rules

findings.finding: The shorthand strings concerning the 2-Influence VP space are disambiguated by the answer-key terminology notes. Read with those notes, the key awards one VP at two Influence and does not assert a two-VP reward.
source_references: Official FAQ p3 Plans Within Plans

rejected_candidates.candidate: A different three-way/four-way Combat tie example or changed strength totals
rejected_candidates.reason: The source-defined tie branches, unavailable ordinary third reward in fewer than four players, zero-strength exclusion, and untied ranks are already explicitly required by Q11/Q20/Q69. Additional arithmetic does not add a rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Unused Agents, empty hand, or exhaustion followed by early Reveal
rejected_candidates.reason: These are applications of Q03/Q04/Q07/Q68. No separate new timing permission or exception is stated.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Move an Agent from Hall of Oratory or a Maker space before Reveal/Makers
rejected_candidates.reason: Q30 already conditions Hall Persuasion on continued Agent presence; Q12 explicitly tests moved-away Maker occupancy. Combining either with Q40 is a mechanical recombination.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Buy a replacement during Reveal, topdeck it with Recruitment Mission, then draw it
rejected_candidates.reason: Interleaving, Row refill, independent acquisition destination, and immediate during-Reveal use are already tested by Q08/Q36/Q54/Q66. This composite invents no new source rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Reserve card is trashed and subsequently acquired again
rejected_candidates.reason: Q16 explicitly requires return to the Reserve stack; Q47 independently preserves the acquired VP. Reusing a returned card is a consequence of the existing destination rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Two-player human starts at zero VP rather than one
rejected_candidates.reason: The source has one common otherwise-zero setup branch and a four-player one-VP exception, already exercised by Q02; substituting two humans for three adds no distinct branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Leader selection can be chosen or random; first-game complexity recommendation; same-House story preference
rejected_candidates.reason: These are setup choice/presentation guidance without a consequential missing procedure. Q23 already states Leader operation, and Q64 establishes actual randomized first-player setup.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Initial Combat marker at zero, marker face/orientation, garrison nearest player, component/deck inventory names
rejected_candidates.reason: These physical setup details do not add an untested consequential rule beyond the tested zero-based strength tracking, human initial army and standard ten-card deck. Excluded as cosmetic/component trivia under the requested novelty threshold.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Apply an opponent-targeting card to a Rival, or make House Hagal occupy a controlled/harvesting space
rejected_candidates.reason: Q17/Q19/Q58 already test controller payout, replacement of ordinary effects, bonus-spice removal, and opponent effect applicability. New named combinations add no rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Harvest Spice card illustration as a source for additional card-selection thresholds
rejected_candidates.reason: The operative p19 instruction is to follow that card and remove bonus spice; Q19 tests the mandatory rule. The low-resolution illustration does not supply a reliably readable additional selection rule, so no unverified card text was invented.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Staged Incident as a separately numbered exception
rejected_candidates.reason: The FAQ explicitly treats it like any other Combat strength adjustment; Q09/Q10 already require that branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Expansion/promo Leaders, grafting, contracts, tech, infiltration, spies, sandworms, solo Rival rewards and Expert deployment
rejected_candidates.reason: These official-FAQ clauses belong to excluded editions/modules/modes and cannot establish a base multiplayer coverage gap.

limitations: This is a source-bounded saturation verdict, not a claim to cover standalone card text absent from the supplied authoritative materials. No additional material was used to invent rules.
